# platform-redis

<!-- Generated by tools/config-reference.py from libs/platform/src/main/resources/META-INF/oidf-settings/platform-redis.json. Do not edit: change the catalogue, then run python3 tools/config-reference.py. -->

The settings of the `platform-redis` component of `libs/platform`, read by package `com.pingidentity.ps.oidf.platform.redis`: generated from its catalogue, [platform-redis.json](../../libs/platform/src/main/resources/META-INF/oidf-settings/platform-redis.json), by `tools/config-reference.py`, and checked in CI. [How to read a row](README.md#reading-a-row).

Families: `OIDF_REDIS_`. A name under one of these that no catalogue declares is an unknown key.

Under the production profile a violation by one of these settings refuses `ATTESTATION_AUTH`, `ATTESTATION_ISSUER`, `OPERATOR_API` ([components](../development/settings-catalogue.md#components)).

| Setting | Default | What it does | When it's wrong | Profile | Security |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `OIDF_REDIS_URL` (system property `oidf.redis.url`, then env `OIDF_REDIS_URL`) | Unset; a secret, never shown | The shared Redis, as redis://[user[:password]@]host[:port][/db] or rediss:// for TLS; unset keeps each store in one node's memory | **First request**: A URL that does not parse, a scheme other than redis or rediss, or redis:// under the production profile: every store that would use Redis refuses its requests, and the log says why without the password. From 0.6.0 a redis:// URL under the production profile also refuses the components that use Redis at start-up | Not in production: a `redis://` URL | Yes |
| `REDIS_URL` | Unset; a secret, never shown | The shared Redis when OIDF_REDIS_URL and its property are unset: the name Railway and most managed Redis providers export; read as OIDF_REDIS_URL is | **First request**: As OIDF_REDIS_URL, when it is read: while OIDF_REDIS_URL or oidf.redis.url is set, REDIS_URL is not read and the production profile does not judge it | Not in production: a `redis://` URL while `OIDF_REDIS_URL` is unset | Yes |
| `OIDF_REDIS_CA_FILE` (system property `oidf.redis.ca.file`, then env `OIDF_REDIS_CA_FILE`) | Unset; a file path | A PEM file of the CA certificates to trust for rediss://, in place of the JVM's; the server's certificate must still name the host | **First request**: A file that cannot be read or holds no certificate: every store that would use Redis refuses its requests, naming the file | Any | Yes |
| `OIDF_REDIS_POOL_SIZE` (system property `oidf.redis.pool.size`, then env `OIDF_REDIS_POOL_SIZE`) | `8`; a whole number, 1 to 256 | The most connections the client holds open at once, in use or idle | **First request**: Not a whole number from 1 to 256 | Any | No |
| `OIDF_REDIS_BORROW_TIMEOUT_MS` (system property `oidf.redis.borrow.timeout.ms`, then env `OIDF_REDIS_BORROW_TIMEOUT_MS`) | `1000`; milliseconds, 1 to 60000 | How long a command waits for a connection when all of them are in use, before it fails as Redis unavailable | **First request**: Not a whole number from 1 to 60000 | Any | No |
| `OIDF_REDIS_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_MS` (system property `oidf.redis.command.timeout.ms`, then env `OIDF_REDIS_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_MS`) | `3000`; milliseconds, 1 to 60000 | How long one command may take once it has a connection: connecting, the TLS handshake, AUTH, finding the master and the one retry included | **First request**: Not a whole number from 1 to 60000 | Any | No |
| `OIDF_REDIS_SENTINEL_MASTER` (system property `oidf.redis.sentinel.master`, then env `OIDF_REDIS_SENTINEL_MASTER`) | Unset | The master's name in Redis Sentinel; set with OIDF_REDIS_SENTINELS, the client asks the sentinels where the master is instead of dialling the URL's host | **First request**: Set without OIDF_REDIS_SENTINELS, or the other way round: every store that would use Redis refuses its requests; a name the sentinels do not know makes every command fail as Redis unavailable | Any | No |
| `OIDF_REDIS_SENTINELS` (system property `oidf.redis.sentinels`, then env `OIDF_REDIS_SENTINELS`) | Unset; a list | The sentinels, as host:port separated by spaces or commas (port 26379 when left out), asked in order; TLS and the CA file apply to them as to the master | **First request**: An entry that is not host or host:port: every store that would use Redis refuses its requests, naming the entry | Any | Yes |
| `OIDF_REDIS_SENTINEL_PASSWORD`; or from the file `OIDF_REDIS_SENTINEL_PASSWORD_FILE` names | Unset; a secret, never shown | The password the sentinels ask for, when they ask for one (the master's comes from the URL) | **First request**: The sentinels refuse AUTH and every command fails as Redis unavailable | Any | Yes |
